breslov.he:
״וַיֵּשֶׁב יַעֲקֹב בְּאֶרֶץ מְגוּרֵי אָבִיו״

(לז, א)

דָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה ׳מְגוּרֵי אָבִיו׳ לְשׁוֹן גֵּרִים שֶׁהָיָה יַעֲקֹב מְגַיֵּר גֵּרִים. וְאִיתָא בִּדְבָרָיו זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בְּסִימָן רכח שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּקֵּשׁ יַעֲקֹב לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה קָפַץ עָלָיו רָגְזוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף, כִּי זֶה שֶׁעוֹסֵק לְגַיֵּר גֵּרִים, בְּהֶכְרֵחַ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ יִסּוּרִים וּמַחֲלֹקֶת וְכוּ׳ וְכֵן הוּא בְּכָל אָדָם.

שֶׁאֵלּוּ הַגֵּרִים וּבַעֲלֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה הָרוֹצִים לָשׁוּב אֶל ה׳ עַל יְדֵי הַצַּדִּיק, בְּהֶכְרֵחַ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עֲלֵיהֶם גַּם כֵּן כַּמָּה מִינֵי מַחֲלֹקֶת וְיִסּוּרִים וְהִתְגַּבְּרוּת וְכוּ׳ בְּכָל פַּעַם, כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְקָרֵב בֶּאֱמֶת לַה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּי אִם עַל יְדֵי זֶה, כַּמְבֹאָר בִּדְבָרֵינוּ הַרְבֵּה בָּזֶה. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר בְּסִימָן ע״ב שֶׁהוּא לְהִתְחַזֵּק בְּכָל פַּעַם כְּנֶגֶד הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וְכוּ׳ עַיֵּן שָׁם.

וְעַל כֵּן עַל כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הָרוֹצֶה לָשׁוּב לַה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ נֶאֱמַר בִּקֵּשׁ יַעֲקֹב לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה קָפַץ עָלָיו וְכוּ׳. וְהַתִּקּוּן לְכָל זֶה הוּא בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף בְּעַצְמוֹ, בִּבְחִינַת אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדוֹת יַעֲקֹב יוֹסֵף, וּפֵרֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י הַפִּשְׁתָּנִי הַזֶּה נִכְנְסוּ גְּמַלָּיו טְעוּנִים פִּשְׁתָּן הַפֶּחָמִי תָּמָה אָנָה יִכְנֹס כָּל הַפִּשְׁתָּן הַזֶּה, הָיָה פִּקֵּחַ אֶחָד הֵשִׁיב לוֹ נִיצוֹץ אֶחָד יוֹצֵא מִמַּפּוּחַ שֶׁלְּךָ שֶׁשּׂוֹרֵף כָּל הַפִּשְׁתָּן, כֵּן וְכוּ׳, וְהָיָה בֵּית יַעֲקֹב אֵשׁ וּבֵית יוֹסֵף לֶהָבָה וּבֵית עֵשָׂו לְקַשׁ נִיצוֹץ יוֹצֵא מִיּוֹסֵף שֶׁמְּכַלֶּה וְשׂוֹרֵף הַכֹּל.

כִּי יַעֲקֹב רָאָה כָּל הָאַלּוּפִים הַכְּתוּבִים לְמַעְלָה תָּמָה וְכוּ׳ מַה כְּתִיב לְמַטָּה אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדוֹת יַעֲקֹב יוֹסֵף וְכוּ׳ נִיצוֹץ אֶחָד וְכוּ׳. וְכֵן פֵּרֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י בְּפָסוּק וַיְהִי כַּאֲשֶׁר יָלְדָה רָחֵל אֶת יוֹסֵף וַיֹּאמֶר שַׁלְּחֵנִי וְכוּ׳ וּפֵרֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י מִשֶּׁנּוֹלַד שִׂטְנוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו וְכוּ׳ אֵין אֵשׁ בְּלֹא לֶהָבָה אֵינוֹ שׁוֹלֵט וְכוּ׳.

הַיְנוּ כִּי יוֹסֵף הוּא בְּחִינַת הַצַּדִּיק הָאֱמֶת שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְשַׂמֵּחַ אֶת לֵב כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל וּלְהַפֵּךְ הַיָּגוֹן וַאֲנָחָה לְשִׂמְחָה, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מַלְהִיב אֶת לֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל לַה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר בְּסִימָן ט בְּלִקּוּטֵי תִּנְיָנָא כִּי הַצַּדִּיק הוּא בְּחִינַת אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר רוּחַ בּוֹ שֶׁמְּנַשֵּׁב הָעַפְרוּרִיּוּת שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת עַצְבוּת, מִלֵּב אִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי, כְּדֵי שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִתְלַהֵב לַה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכוּ׳ עַיֵּן שָׁם.

וְזֶה בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ הֲנִמְצָא כָּזֶה אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר רוּחַ אֱלֹקִים בּוֹ, כִּי יוֹסֵף הוּא בְּחִינַת הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁיָּכוֹל לֵירֵד לְתוֹךְ כָּל הֵיכְלֵי הַתְּמוּרוֹת וּלְהוֹצִיא כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִשָּׁם, כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מֵעֹמֶק נְפִילָתוֹ, כָּל מִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לְהִתְאַחֵז בּוֹ, כִּי בְּוַדַּאי מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה כְּלָל מִכָּל שֶׁכֵּן כְּשֶׁחוֹלֵק וְכוּ׳ בְּוַדַּאי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲזֹר לוֹ, וְעָלָיו נֶאֱמַר בְּאָזְנֵי כְסִיל אַל תְּדַבֵּר כִּי יָבוּז לְשֵׂכֶל מִלֶּיךָ, אֲבָל כָּל מִי שֶׁחָס עַל נַפְשׁוֹ עֲדַיִן וְחָפֵץ בְּחַיִּים אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנָּפַל כְּמוֹ שֶׁנָּפַל, יָכוֹל הַצַּדִּיק בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף לְהוֹצִיאוֹ מִשָּׁם.

כִּי יוֹסֵף יָרַד לְכָל הֵיכְלֵי הַתְּמוּרוֹת, בִּבְחִינַת לְעֶבֶד נִמְכַּר יוֹסֵף, עַבְדוּת בְּחִינַת עַצְבוּת כַּמּוּבָא בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר, שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ מִזֻּהֲמַת הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת חָם שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ יָצָא מִצְרַיִם שֶׁנִּתְקַלֵּל עֶבֶד עֲבָדִים יִהְיֶה וְכוּ׳ כַּמּוּבָא, וְיוֹסֵף עָבַר בְּכָל זֶה וְהָיָה לוֹ נִסְיוֹנוֹת עֲצוּמִים בְּתַאֲוָה זֹאת שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ מֵעַצְבוּת, וְהָיָה בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִים כַּמָּה שָׁנִים, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה עָבַר בְּכָל בְּחִינוֹת הֵיכְלֵי הַתְּמוּרוֹת וְיָצָא מֵהֶם בְּשָׁלוֹם, אַף גַּם זָכָה לְתוֹסֶפֶת קְדֻשָּׁה עֲצוּמָה עַל יְדֵי זֶה, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת ׳יוֹסֵף יוֹסֵף׳ בְּחִינַת יִשְׁמַע חָכָם וְיוֹסֵף לֶקַח. וְעַל כֵּן יֵשׁ לוֹ כֹּחַ לְהַפֵּךְ הַכֹּל לְטוֹבָה לְהַפֵּךְ הַיָּגוֹן וַאֲנָחָה לְשִׂמְחָה.

שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת מַה שֶּׁהִתְנַבְּאָה רָחֵל כַּאֲשֶׁר נוֹלַד יוֹסֵף וְאָמְרָה אָסַף אֱלֹקִים אֶת חֶרְפָּתִי, כִּי עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁיָּכוֹל לַעֲבֹר בְּכָל הֵיכְלֵי הַתְּמוּרוֹת וְלָצֵאת מִשָּׁם בְּשָׁלוֹם עַל יְדֵי זֶה יִתְבַּטְּלוּ כָּל הַחֲרָפוֹת הַבָּאִין מִשָּׁם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ קָרְאָה שְׁמוֹ יוֹסֵף לֵאמֹר יוֹסֵף ה׳ לִי בֵּן אַחֵר, הַיְנוּ שֶׁאָמְרָה שֶׁלֹּא דַּי שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ יִתְבַּטְּלוּ הַחֲרָפוֹת בְּחִינַת אָסַף אֱלֹקִים אֶת חֶרְפָּתִי, אַף גַּם יִהְיֶה לוֹ כֹּחַ לְהַפֵּךְ הַחֲרָפוֹת לְכָבוֹד לְהַפֵּךְ הַיָּגוֹן וַאֲנָחָה לְשִׂמְחָה שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף ה׳ לִי בֵּן אַחֵר, בְּחִינַת מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים הַמְּשַׂמְּחִים הַלֵּב בְּחִינַת בֵּן חָכָם יְשַׂמַּח אָב, כִּי עִקַּר תּוֹלְדוֹתֵיהֶן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים הֵם מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים, הַיְנוּ שֶׁדַּיְקָא עַל יְדֵי הַחֲרָפוֹת וְכוּ׳ יוֹסֵף בֵּן אַחֵר שֶׁהוּא תּוֹלָדָה דִּקְדֻשָּׁה לְהוֹסִיף וּלְהוֹלִיד עַל יְדֵי זֶה דַּיְקָא שִׂמְחָה וְטוֹב בִּבְחִינַת הִתְהַפְּכוּת הַיָּגוֹן וַאֲנָחָה לְשִׂמְחָה.

שֶׁכָּל זֶה בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב ׳לְמִחְיָה שְׁלָחַנִי אֱלֹקִים לִפְנֵיכֶם׳ וְכוּ׳, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב ׳וְאַתֶּם חֲשַׁבְתֶּם לְרָעָה אֱלֹקִים חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטֹבָה לְמַעַן עֲשֹׂה כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה לְהַחֲיֹת עַם רָב׳. וְאִיתָא בְּסְפָרִים עַל זֶה, אַשְׁרֵיהֶם בַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה כִּי לְמִחְיָה שְׁלָחַנִי אֱלֹקִים וְכוּ׳. וּלְשָׁם הַמְּקוֹמוֹת אֲשֶׁר נָפְצוּ שָׁם לְקָרֵב נִיצוֹצֵי קְדֻשָּׁה לִמְקוֹמָם וְכוּ׳, שֶׁכָּל זֶה בְּחִינַת יְרִידָה תַּכְלִית הָעֲלִיָּה בִּבְחִינַת הַנַּ״ל שֶׁנִּתְהַפֵּךְ הַכֹּל לְטוֹבָה לְשָׂשׂוֹן וְשִׂמְחָה וְכַנַּ״ל. וְעַל כֵּן דַּיְקָא בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף יָכוֹל לְהַלְהִיב אֶת הַלֵּב לַה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִשְׂרֹף אֶת כָּל בְּחִינַת אַלּוּפֵי עֵשָׂו וְיַהֲפֹךְ הַכֹּל לְשִׂמְחָה וּלְטוֹבָה.

וְזֶה ׳וַיֵּשֶׁב יַעֲקֹב וַיֵּשֶׁב׳ דַּיְקָא, בְּחִינַת מֹחַ הַמְסֻדָּר וְהַמְיֻשָּׁב שֶׁזָּכָה יַעֲקֹב בְּחִינַת הַשֵּׂכֶל הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁרוֹדֵף תָּמִיד לְהַשִּׂיג הָאוֹר אֵין סוֹף וְכוּ׳ כַּנַּ״ל, כִּי הַשֵּׂכֶל נִקְרָא יַעֲקֹב כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים. וְזֶה וַיֵּשֶׁב יַעֲקֹב שֶׁזָּכָה לִבְחִינַת הַמְסֻדָּר וְהַמְיֻשָּׁב. וְזֶה בְּאֶרֶץ מְגוּרֵי אָבִיו עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהָיָה מְגַיֵּר גֵּרִים שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת מִי יִמָּר הַנַּ״ל שֶׁיָּכוֹל לֵירֵד לְהֵיכְלֵי הַתְּמוּרוֹת וְכוּ׳. אַךְ בְּכָל פַּעַם מִתְגָּרִים בּוֹ וְהַנִּלְוִים אֵלָיו מְאֹד מְאֹד וּמַנִּיחִים אוֹתוֹ וְכוּ׳ לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה כַּנַּ״ל. וְהַתִּקּוּן לְזֶה הוּא אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדוֹת יַעֲקֹב יוֹסֵף וְכוּ׳, שֶׁהַצַּדִּיק בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב בְּחִינַת הַשֵּׂכֶל הַקָּדוֹשׁ מוֹלִיד בִּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת תּוֹסֶפֶת קְדֻשָּׁה בְּכָל פַּעַם, כִּי אֵינוֹ נוֹפֵל לְזִקְנָה דְּסִטְרָא אַחֲרָא בְּשׁוּם אֹפֶן, רַק הוּא מוֹסִיף קְדֻשָּׁה וָדַעַת בְּכָל פַּעַם עַד שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְהַפֵּךְ כָּל הַיָּגוֹן וַאֲנָחָה לְשִׂמְחָה, בִּבְחִינַת ׳יוֹסֵף עֲדֵינָה בְּשִׂמְחָה׳ וְכוּ׳.

וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשֶׂה בְּחִינַת בֵּית יוֹסֵף לֶהָבָה שֶׁמַּלְהִיב אֵשׁ הַקְּדֻשָּׁה שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב כִּי הוּא אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר רוּחַ אֱלֹקִים בּוֹ שֶׁמְּנַשֵּׁב הָעַפְרוּרִיּוּת מִכָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל כַּנַּ״ל, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִיצוֹץ אֶחָד יוֹצֵא מִבְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף שֶׁשּׂוֹרֵף אֶת כָּל אַלּוּפֵי עֵשָׂו שֶׁהֵם כְּלַל כָּל הַמְּנִיעוֹת וְהַסִּטְרִין אַחֲרָנִין שֶׁמֵּהֶם כָּל הָעַצְבוּת וְהַחֲלִישׁוּת הַדַּעַת וְהַהִתְגַּבְּרוּת וְכוּ׳ וְכוּ׳ שֶׁמִּתְגַּבֵּר עַל כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד, כִּי עַל יְדֵי נִיצוֹץ אֶחָד שֶׁל אוֹר הָאֱמֶת שֶׁמַּכְנִיס בְּלֵב אִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי עַד שֶׁמַּלְהִיב אֶת לִבּוֹ לַה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ, עַל יְדֵי זֶה מְכַלֶּה וְשׂוֹרֵף אֶת כָּל הַמּוֹנְעִים וְכוּ׳.

וְזֶה ׳וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אָהַב אֶת יוֹסֵף מִכָּל בָּנָיו כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ׳. זְקֻנִים לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים, כִּי הוּא עוֹסֵק תָּמִיד לְהַגְבִּיר בְּכָל פַּעַם הַזִּקְנָה דִּקְדֻשָּׁה עַל בְּחִינַת הַזִּקְנָה דְּסִטְרָא אַחֲרָא, כִּי יֵשׁ זָקֵן דְּסִטְרָא אַחֲרָא שֶׁעוֹסֵק תָּמִיד לְהַפִּיל אֶת הָאָדָם לִידֵי זִקְנָה הַיְנוּ לְהַחֲלִישׁ אֶת דַּעְתּוֹ כְּאִלּוּ הוּא זָקֵן בְּמַעֲשָׂיו וְכוּ׳, שֶׁעַל זֶה הִזְהִיר אֲדוֹנֵנוּ מוֹרֵנוּ וְרַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה וְכֵן שָׁמַעְנוּ מִכַּמָּה צַדִּיקִים שֶׁאָסוּר לִהְיוֹת זָקֵן וְכוּ׳, וּמַכְנִיעוֹ עַל יְדֵי זָקֵן דִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת זָקֵן וְיוֹשֵׁב בִּישִׁיבָה הָאֲמִתִּי בְּחִינַת זָקֵן זֶה קָנָה חָכְמָה, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא מוֹסִיף קְדֻשָּׁה וְחִיּוּת בְּכָל פַּעַם וְכַנַּ״ל. וּכְבָר מְבֹאָר מִזֶּה בִּדְבָרֵינוּ הַרְבֵּה (ועיין בהלכות תפילין הלכה ה).

וְזֶה בְּחִינַת ׳כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ׳ לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים, שֶׁבְּכָל פַּעַם מוֹסִיף זִקְנָה דִּקְדֻשָּׁה עַל זִקְנָה דִּקְדֻשָּׁה, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת וְיִרְאַת ה׳ מוֹסִיף יָמִים, לְהַכְנִיעַ וּלְבַטֵּל בְּחִינַת זָקֵן דְּסִטְרָא אַחֲרָא שֶׁעַל זֶה הִתְפַּלֵּל דָּוִד אַל תַּשְׁלִיכֵנִי לְעֵת זִקְנָה וְכוּ׳. כִּי צְרִיכִין לְהִתְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל פַּעַם מֵחָדָשׁ בִּבְחִינַת וְקוֹיֵ ה׳ יַחֲלִיפוּ כֹחַ וְכוּ׳ שֶׁזֶּה עִקַּר בְּחִינַת זִקְנָה דִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁנִּקְרָא עַל שֵׁם זֶה יוֹסֵף עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהוּא מוֹסִיף קְדֻשָּׁה וָדַעַת שֶׁהוּא עִקַּר הַחִיּוּת בְּכָל פַּעַם וְכַנַּ״ל.

(הלכות ברכת הודאה הלכה ו׳ אות ל״ב)
breslov.en:
“And Yaakov dwelt in the land of his father’s sojournings.”

(37:1)

Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded in Midrash Rabbah “his father’s sojournings” as an expression of converts, for Yaakov would convert converts. And it is stated in his words, of blessed memory, in section 228 [candidate printed numeral רכח], that this is the aspect of what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: Yaakov wished to dwell in tranquility; the trouble of Yosef sprang upon him. For one who occupies himself with converting converts necessarily has suffering and dispute, etc.; and so it is with every person.

For these converts and penitents who wish to return to the Lord through the tzaddik necessarily also undergo several kinds of dispute, suffering, and overpowering, etc., each time. For it is impossible to draw near in truth to the Lord, blessed be He, except through this, as explained at length in our words on this. And as explained in section 72, which is to strengthen oneself each time against the evil inclination, etc.; see there.

And therefore concerning each and every person of Israel who wishes to return to the Lord, blessed be He, it is said: Yaakov wished to dwell in tranquility; there sprang upon him, etc. And the rectification for all this is the aspect of Yosef himself, in the aspect of “These are the offspring of Yaakov: Yosef.” And Rash״i explained: This flax dealer’s camels came in laden with flax; the charcoal burner wondered, where will all this flax enter? One discerning person answered him: one spark comes out of your bellows that burns all the flax. So, etc., “And the house of Yaakov shall be fire, and the house of Yosef a flame, and the house of Esav straw”: a spark comes out of Yosef that consumes and burns everything.

For Yaakov saw all the chieftains written above and wondered, etc. What is written below? “These are the offspring of Yaakov: Yosef,” etc.—one spark, etc. And likewise Rash״i explained concerning the verse “And it was when Rachel bore Yosef, and he said, ‘Send me away,’” etc. Rash״i explained: once Esav’s antagonist was born, etc.; fire without a flame does not rule, etc.

Namely, Yosef is the aspect of the true tzaddik who can gladden the heart of each person of Israel and turn sorrow and sighing into joy, through which he sets the heart of Israel aflame toward the Lord, blessed be He. And as explained in section 9 of Likutay Tinyana, the tzaddik is the aspect of “a man in whom there is spirit,” who blows away the dustiness, which is the aspect of sadness, from the heart of an Israelite person, so that he can be set aflame toward the Lord, blessed be He, etc.; see there.

And this is the aspect of Yosef, concerning whom it is said: “Can there be found such a man in whom there is the spirit of God?” For Yosef is the aspect of the tzaddik who can descend into all the chambers of exchanges and bring out all the souls from there, each and every one from the depth of his fall, anyone who wishes to hold onto him. For certainly one who does not wish at all, and all the more so when he disputes, etc., certainly cannot be helped; and concerning him it is said, “Do not speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the intellect of your words.” But anyone who still has compassion on his soul and desires life, even though he has fallen as he has fallen, the tzaddik, the aspect of Yosef, can bring him out from there.

For Yosef descended into all the chambers of exchanges, in the aspect of “Yosef was sold as a slave”—slavery being the aspect of sadness, as cited elsewhere, which is drawn from the filth of the serpent, which is the aspect of Cham, from whom Egypt came forth, who was cursed, “A slave of slaves he shall be,” etc., as cited. And Yosef passed through all this and had immense trials in this desire, which is drawn from sadness, and was in prison for several years. And through this he passed through all the aspects of the chambers of exchanges and came out of them in peace; indeed, he also attained an immense addition of holiness through this. This is the aspect of “Yosef, Yosef,” the aspect of “A wise man shall hear and add learning.” And therefore he has the power to turn everything to good, to turn sorrow and sighing into joy.

This is the aspect of what Rachel prophesied when Yosef was born, saying “God has gathered away my reproach.” For through the aspect of Yosef the tzaddik, who can pass through all the chambers of exchanges and come out of there in peace, through this all the reproaches coming from there will be nullified. And afterwards she called his name Yosef, saying “May the Lord add another son for me.” Namely, she said that it was not enough that through him the reproaches should be nullified, the aspect of “God has gathered away my reproach”; rather, he would also have the power to turn the reproaches into honor, to turn sorrow and sighing into joy. This is the aspect of “May the Lord add another son for me,” the aspect of good deeds that gladden the heart, the aspect of “A wise son shall gladden a father.” For the principal offspring of tzaddikim are good deeds. Namely, specifically through the reproaches, etc., another son shall be added, who is a holy offspring, to add and bring forth through this specifically joy and goodness, in the aspect of turning sorrow and sighing into joy.

For all this is the aspect of Yosef, as it is written, “God sent me before you for preservation of life,” etc.; and as it is written, “And you intended evil, but God intended it for good, in order to do as on this day, to keep a numerous people alive.” And it is stated in books concerning this: fortunate are the penitents, for “God sent me for preservation of life,” etc. And to those places where they were scattered, to draw sparks of holiness near to their place, etc. All this is the aspect of descent for the ultimate purpose of ascent, in the aspect mentioned above, that everything is turned to good, to gladness and joy, as above. And therefore specifically the aspect of Yosef can set the heart aflame toward the Lord, blessed be He, and through this burn all the aspect of Esav’s chieftains and turn everything to joy and good.

And this is “And Yaakov dwelt”—“dwelt” specifically, the aspect of the ordered and settled mind that Yaakov attained, the aspect of the holy intellect which continually pursues the apprehension of the light of the Infinite, etc., as above. For intellect is called Yaakov, as explained several times. And this is “And Yaakov dwelt”: he attained the aspect of being ordered and settled. And this is “in the land of his father’s sojournings,” through his converting converts, which is the aspect of the “mi yimmar” mentioned above [candidate technical phrase, unresolved], who can descend to the chambers of exchanges, etc. But each time they provoke him and those accompanying him very, very much, and leave him, etc., to dwell in tranquility, as above. And the rectification for this is “These are the offspring of Yaakov: Yosef,” etc.: that the tzaddik, the aspect of Yaakov, the aspect of the holy intellect, brings forth in his holiness the aspect of Yosef, which is the aspect of an addition of holiness each time. For he does not fall into old age of the other side in any manner; rather, he adds holiness and understanding each time, until he can turn all sorrow and sighing into joy, in the aspect of “Yosef adinah with joy” [candidate quoted phrase, unresolved], etc.

And through this the aspect of the house of Yosef as a flame is made, which sets aflame Yaakov’s fire of holiness, for he is a man in whom there is the spirit of God, who blows away the dustiness from every person of Israel, as above. And through this one spark goes out from the aspect of Yosef that burns all of Esav’s chieftains, which are the totality of all the impediments and the other sides, from which come all the sadness, discouragement, and overpowering, etc., etc., that overpower each and every person. For through one spark of the light of truth that he brings into the heart of an Israelite person until he sets his heart aflame toward the Lord, blessed be He, through this he consumes and burns all those that prevent, etc.

And this is “And Israel loved Yosef more than all his sons, for he was a son of old age to him.” Zekunim is a plural expression, for he continually occupies himself with strengthening, each time, holy old age over the aspect of old age of the other side. For there is an elder of the other side who continually occupies himself with bringing a person down into old age—namely, weakening his understanding as though he were old in his deeds, etc. Concerning this our master, teacher, and Rabbainu, of blessed memory, warned, and likewise we have heard from several tzaddikim, that it is forbidden to be old, etc. And he subdues it through the holy elder, who is the aspect of the true elder who sits in the academy, the aspect of “elder—this one acquired wisdom,” which is the aspect of Yosef, who adds holiness and vitality each time, as above. And much of this has already been explained in our words (and see Halachos of Tefillin, Halacha 5).

And this is the aspect of “For he was a son of old age to him,” a plural expression: each time he adds holy old age upon holy old age—which is the aspect of “And the fear of the Lord adds days,” to subdue and nullify the aspect of the elder of the other side, concerning which Dovid prayed, “Do not cast me away at the time of old age,” etc. For one needs to renew oneself anew each time, in the aspect of “And those who hope in the Lord shall renew their strength,” etc. This is the principal aspect of holy old age, which is the aspect of Yosef the tzaddik, who is called Yosef on account of this, on account of his adding holiness and understanding, which is the principal vitality, each time, as above.

(Halachos of the Blessing of Thanksgiving, Halacha 6, item 32)

pairs.en: “And Yaakov dwelt,” etc.: he wished to dwell in tranquility, for he thought that, since he had already subdued the aspect of Lavan and Esav and had been delivered from them, who are the principal aspect of the opponents, henceforth he would dwell in tranquility. But the trouble of Yosef sprang upon him, which is the aspect of dispute among Israel and among the tzaddikim themselves. This was the aspect of the dispute of the tribes against Yosef the tzaddik.

״וַיֵּשֶׁב יַעֲקֹב בְּאֶרֶץ מְגוּרֵי אָבִיו״

(לז, א)

pairs.en: The principal prevailing of the soiled garments is in the desire for sexual immorality; and Yosef, who stripped this from himself entirely, merited the striped tunic.

pairs.en: Yosef attained completely to stripping the soiled garments from himself through standing in the trial involving a menstruant woman, a bondwoman, a gentile woman, a harlot, from which the soiled garments chiefly come. And Yaakov our father, because he saw Yosef’s righteousness, therefore “made him a striped tunic,” the aspect of fine garments, clean garments. And this is “For he was a son of old age to him, and he made him a striped tunic.” For the one depends on the other [following the cited source; the anthology’s Hebrew differs]: because he had a son of old age, a wise son, to whom he transmitted all that he had received from Shem and Ever—namely, he transmitted all his wisdom and Torah to him—therefore “he made him a striped tunic,” the aspect of חלוקא דרבנן [the sages’ garment], the aspect of clean garments that are attained through Torah.

And Yaakov our father, because he saw Yosef’s righteousness, therefore “made him a striped tunic,” the aspect of fine garments, clean garments. And this is “For he was a son of old age to him, and he made him a striped tunic.” For the one depends on the other [following the cited source; the anthology’s Hebrew differs]: because he had a son of old age, a wise son, to whom he transmitted all that he had received from Shem and Ever—namely, he transmitted all his wisdom and Torah to him—therefore “he made him a striped tunic,” the aspect of חלוקא דרבנן [the sages’ garment], the aspect of clean garments that are attained through Torah.

pairs.he: אֲבָל אֶחָיו נִתְקַנְּאוּ בּוֹ בָּזֶה. וְגַם רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה הִקְפִּידוּ עַל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ בָּזֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שבת דף י) ׳לְעוֹלָם אַל יְשַׁנֶּה אָדָם בְּנוֹ וְכוּ׳ שֶׁבִּשְׁבִיל מִשְׁקַל שְׁתֵּי סְלָעִים מֵילַת נִתְגַּלְגֵּל הַדָּבָר וְכוּ׳. הַיְנוּ שֶׁעֲדַיִן הָיָה קֹדֶם הַזְּמַן. כִּי עֲדַיִן הָיָה צָרִיךְ לַעֲבֹר עַל יוֹסֵף מַה שֶּׁעָבַר נִסְיוֹנוֹת רַבּוֹת. וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה צָרִיךְ לְהַמְתִּין מִלְּהַלְבִּישׁוֹ בִּכְתֹנֶת פַּסִּים עַד שֶׁיְּזַכֵּךְ עַצְמוֹ בִּשְׁלֵמוּת מִבְּחִינַת אֲחִיזַת הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיַּעֲבֹר בְּנִסָּיוֹן.
pairs.en: But his brothers envied him in this. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, also took issue with Yaakov our father about this, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Shabbos, folio 10), “A person should never treat his son differently,” etc., “for because of the weight of two selaim of fine wool the matter unfolded,” etc. Namely, it was still before the time, for what passed over Yosef—many trials—still had to pass over him. And therefore he needed to wait before clothing him in a striped tunic until [Yosef] purified himself completely from the aspect of the hold of the soiled garments through undergoing the trial.

pairs.he: אחיו סברו שאינו נקי מזה ולכן התקנאו בזה והפשיטו ממנו כתנת זו
pairs.en: His brothers thought that he was not clean of this; and therefore they envied him in this and stripped this tunic from him.

qualifiedAfter.he: אחיו סברו שאינו נקי מזה ולכן התקנאו בזה והפשיטו ממנו כתנת זו

pairs.he: וּבִשְׁבִיל זֶה נִתְקַנְּאוּ בוֹ אֶחָיו, כִּי גַּם הֵם הָיוּ בַּעֲלֵי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְרָאוּ שֶׁעֲדַיִן הַבַּעַל דָּבָר מִתְגָּרֶה בּוֹ וְטָעוּ וְסָבְרוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ נָקִי כְּלָל מֵאֲחִיזַת הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים עַל כֵּן נִתְקַנְּאוּ עַל שֶׁעָשָׂה לוֹ אָבִיו כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים.
pairs.en: And because of this his brothers envied him, for they too possessed the holy spirit and saw that the adversary was still provoking him, and they erred and thought that he was not at all clean of the hold of the soiled garments. Therefore they envied him because his father had made him a striped tunic.

Therefore they envied him because his father had made him a striped tunic.

pairs.he: וְעַל כֵּן ״וַיַּפְשִׁיטוּ אֶת יוֹסֵף אֶת כֻּתָּנְתּוֹ אֶת כְּתֹנֶת הַפַּסִּים וְכוּ׳ וַיִּטְבְּלוּ אוֹתוֹ בְּדָם״, לְהוֹרוֹת שֶׁעֲדַיִן יֵשׁ בּוֹ אֲחִיזַת הַקִּלְקוּלִים הַנִּמְשָׁכִין מֵהַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים.
pairs.en: And therefore “and they stripped Yosef of his tunic, the striped tunic,” etc., “and dipped it in blood,” to indicate that he still had in him a hold of the corruptions that are drawn from the soiled garments.

qualifiedAfter.en: And therefore “and they stripped Yosef of his tunic, the striped tunic,” etc., “and dipped it in blood,” to indicate that he still had in him a hold of the corruptions that are drawn from the soiled garments.

pairs.he: ולכן כשהביאו את הכתנת ליעקב מיד קשר את זה למלחמת אשת פוטיפר
pairs.en: And therefore, when they brought the tunic to Yaakov, he immediately connected this to the battle involving Potiphar’s wife.

qualifiedAfter.he: ולכן כשהביאו את הכתנת ליעקב מיד קשר את זה למלחמת אשת פוטיפר
qualifiedAfter.en: And therefore, when they brought the tunic to Yaakov, he immediately connected this to the battle involving Potiphar’s wife.

pairs.he: וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁהֵבִיאוּ אֶת הַכְּתֹנֶת הַמְלֻכְלֶכֶת בְּדָם אֶל יַעֲקֹב אֲבִיהֶם, עַל כֵּן וַיֵּדַע יַעֲקֹב שֶׁמַּלְבּוּשׁ שָׁם בִּכְתָנָיו וְכוּ׳. וְאָז אָמַר, ״כְּתֹנֶת בְּנִי חַיָּה רָעָה אֲכָלָתְהוּ וְכוּ׳״ וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁנִּרְמַז שֶׁמִּתְגָּרֶה בּוֹ אִשָּׁה פּוֹטִיפַר. וְלִכְאוֹרָה תָּמוּהַּ הָעִנְיַן זֶה אֵצֶל זֶה, מַה עִנְיַן סְמִיכוֹת ״כְּתֹנֶת בְּנִי לְחַיָּה רָעָה אֲכָלָתְהוּ״ שֶׁהוּא עַל הִתְגָּרוּת אֵשֶׁת פּוֹטִיפַר.
pairs.en: And therefore, when they brought the blood-soiled tunic to Yaakov their father, therefore “and Yaakov tore his garments and put sackcloth on his loins,” etc. And then he said, “My son’s tunic—a wild animal has devoured him,” etc. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded that it was hinted that Potiphar’s wife was provoking him. And at first sight the placement of this matter beside that is puzzling: what is the matter of the juxtaposition of “my son’s tunic” to “a wild animal has devoured him,” which concerns the provocation of Potiphar’s wife?

qualifiedAfter.en: And therefore, when they brought the blood-soiled tunic to Yaakov their father, therefore “and Yaakov tore his garments and put sackcloth on his loins,” etc. And then he said, “My son’s tunic—a wild animal has devoured him,” etc. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded that it was hinted that Potiphar’s wife was provoking him. And at first sight the placement of this matter beside that is puzzling: what is the matter of the juxtaposition of “my son’s tunic” to “a wild animal has devoured him,” which concerns the provocation of Potiphar’s wife?

pairs.he: אַךְ עַל פִּי הַנַּ״ל מְבֹאָר הֵיטֵב. כִּי תֵּכֶף כְּשֶׁרָאָה שֶׁכְּתֹנֶת יוֹסֵף מְלֻכְלֶכֶת בְּדָם אָז הֵבִין שֶׁעֲדַיִן מִתְגָּרִין בּוֹ הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים, שֶׁעִקַּר הִתְגָּרוּתָם בָּאָדָם הוּא בְּתַאֲוַת נִאוּף. וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר אָז כְּתֹנֶת בְּנִי חַיָּה רָעָה אֲכָלָתְהוּ שֶׁהִיא הִתְגָּרוּת אֵשֶׁת פּוֹטִיפַר שֶׁהִיא נִדָּה שִׁפְחָה גּוֹיָה זוֹנָה, שֶׁהֵם עִקַּר הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: But according to the above it is clearly explained. For immediately when he saw that Yosef’s tunic was soiled with blood, he understood that the soiled garments were still provoking him, for their principal provocation of a person is in the desire for sexual immorality. And therefore he then said, “My son’s tunic—a wild animal has devoured him,” which is the provocation of Potiphar’s wife, who is a menstruant woman, a bondwoman, a gentile woman, a harlot, which are the principal soiled garments, as above.

pairs.he: וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם בְּעֵת הַנִּסָּיוֹן וַתִּתְפְּשֵׂהוּ בְּבִגְדוֹ. ׳בִּבְגְדוֹ׳ דַּיְקָא, כִּי רָצְתָה לְהִתְאַחֵז בְּבִגְדוֹ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְלַבֵּשׁ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בְּבְגָדִים צוֹאִים, אֲבָל יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק עָמַד בְּנִסָּיוֹן וְלֹא רָצָה לְטַמֹּאות נִשְׁמָתוֹ עַל יְדֵי בְּגָדִים צוֹאִים הַנִּמְשָׁכִין עַל יְדֵי נִאוּף. וְעַל כֵּן ״וַיַּעֲזֹב בִּגְדוֹ בְּיָדָהּ וַיָּנָס וַיֵּצֵא הַחוּצָה״. וְאָז דַּיְקָא בְּאוֹתָהּ הָרֶגַע הִפְשִׁיט מֵעַצְמוֹ בִּשְׁלֵמוּת כָּל אֲחִיזַת הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים שֶׁהָיוּ נֶאֱחָזִין בִּבְגָדָיו. כִּי אֲפִלּוּ הַצַּדִּיקִים הַגְּדוֹלִים כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא עָמְדוּ בַּנִּסָּיוֹן כָּרָאוּי לָהֶם עֲדַיִן יֵשׁ בָּהֶם אֵיזֶה אֲחִיזָה מֵהַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים. וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁעָבַר יוֹסֵף בַּנִּסָּיוֹן אָז דַּיְקָא הִפְשִׁיט מֵעַצְמוֹ בְּחִינַת אֲחִיזַת הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים בִּבְחִינַת וַיַּעֲזֹב בִּגְדוֹ בְּיָדָהּ וַיָּנָס וְכוּ׳. שֶׁהַבֶּגֶד שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ אֲחִיזָה בּוֹ עָזַב בְּיָדָהּ, וְהִפְשִׁיט אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִבְּגָדִים אֵלּוּ בִּשְׁלֵמוּת.
pairs.en: And this is what is written there at the time of the trial: “And she seized him by his garment.” “By his garment” specifically, for she wanted to gain a hold upon his garment, Heaven forbid, so that he would clothe himself, Heaven forbid, in soiled garments. But Yosef the tzaddik stood in the trial and did not want to defile his soul through soiled garments drawn through sexual immorality. And therefore “and he left his garment in her hand, and fled and went outside.” And then specifically, at that moment, he stripped from himself completely every hold of the soiled garments that had held onto his garments. For even the great tzaddikim, as long as they have not stood in the trial as is fitting for them, still have some hold of the soiled garments in them. And therefore, when Yosef passed through the trial, then specifically he stripped from himself the aspect of the hold of the soiled garments, in the aspect of “and he left his garment in her hand and fled,” etc. For the garment upon which she had a hold he left in her hand, and he stripped himself of these garments completely.

pairs.he: וְאָז זָכָה אַחַר כָּךְ לִבְגָדִים נְקִיִּים וִיקָרִים בִּבְחִינַת ״וַיַּלְבֵּשׁ אוֹתוֹ בִּגְדֵי שֵׁשׁ וְכוּ׳״. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ יוֹסֵף מִדִּלֵּהּ נָטַל וְכוּ׳. וּמִגֹּדֶל עֹצֶם צִדְקָתוֹ שֶׁעָמַד בַּנִּסָּיוֹן בָּזֶה זָכָה לְהַמְשִׁיךְ בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים לְכָל אֶחָיו בִּבְחִינַת לְכֻלָּם נָתַן לָאִישׁ חֲלִפוֹת שְׂמָלֹת וְכוּ׳. שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ כֹּחַ לְתַקֵּן כֻּלָּם לְהַמְשִׁיךְ לָהֶם בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים. וְעַל כֵּן וּלְבִנְיָמִן נָתַן וְכוּ׳ וְחָמֵשׁ חֲלִפֹת שְׂמָלֹת, שֶׁנִּרְמַז עַל בִּגְדֵי כֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁהָיָה מַחֲלִיף בְּגָדָיו חֲמִשָּׁה פְּעָמִים בְּיוֹם כִּפּוּר כְּשֶׁנִּכְנַס לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁהָיָה בָּנוּי בְּחֶלְקוֹ כַּמּוּבָא. כִּי עִקַּר בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים בְּגָדִים לְבָנִים זָכָה הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל. שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה מְכַפֵּר עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכַנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And then afterwards he attained clean and precious garments, in the aspect of “he clothed him in linen garments,” etc. And as is stated in the holy Zohar, “Yosef took from his own,” etc. And from the greatness of the might of his righteousness, that he stood in this trial, he attained to drawing the aspect of clean garments to all his brothers, in the aspect of “to all of them he gave each man changes of garments,” etc. This alludes to his having the power to rectify them all, to draw to them the aspect of clean garments. Therefore “and to Binyamin he gave,” etc., “five changes of garments,” which hints at the garments of the High Priest, who changed his garments five times on the Day of Atonement when he entered the Temple, which was built in his portion, as cited. For the High Priest attained the principal aspect of clean garments, white garments. Through this he would atone for all Israel, as above.

qualifiedAfter.he: וְאָז זָכָה אַחַר כָּךְ לִבְגָדִים נְקִיִּים וִיקָרִים בִּבְחִינַת ״וַיַּלְבֵּשׁ אוֹתוֹ בִּגְדֵי שֵׁשׁ וְכוּ׳״. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ יוֹסֵף מִדִּלֵּהּ נָטַל וְכוּ׳. וּמִגֹּדֶל עֹצֶם צִדְקָתוֹ שֶׁעָמַד בַּנִּסָּיוֹן בָּזֶה זָכָה לְהַמְשִׁיךְ בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים לְכָל אֶחָיו בִּבְחִינַת לְכֻלָּם נָתַן לָאִישׁ חֲלִפוֹת שְׂמָלֹת וְכוּ׳. שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ כֹּחַ לְתַקֵּן כֻּלָּם לְהַמְשִׁיךְ לָהֶם בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים. וְעַל כֵּן וּלְבִנְיָמִן נָתַן וְכוּ׳ וְחָמֵשׁ חֲלִפֹת שְׂמָלֹת, שֶׁנִּרְמַז עַל בִּגְדֵי כֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁהָיָה מַחֲלִיף בְּגָדָיו חֲמִשָּׁה פְּעָמִים בְּיוֹם כִּפּוּר כְּשֶׁנִּכְנַס לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁהָיָה בָּנוּי בְּחֶלְקוֹ כַּמּוּבָא. כִּי עִקַּר בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים בְּגָדִים לְבָנִים זָכָה הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל. שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה מְכַפֵּר עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכַנַּ״ל.
qualifiedAfter.en: And then afterwards he attained clean and precious garments, in the aspect of “he clothed him in linen garments,” etc. And as is stated in the holy Zohar, “Yosef took from his own,” etc. And from the greatness of the might of his righteousness, that he stood in this trial, he attained to drawing the aspect of clean garments to all his brothers, in the aspect of “to all of them he gave each man changes of garments,” etc. This alludes to his having the power to rectify them all, to draw to them the aspect of clean garments. Therefore “and to Binyamin he gave,” etc., “five changes of garments,” which hints at the garments of the High Priest, who changed his garments five times on the Day of Atonement when he entered the Temple, which was built in his portion, as cited. For the High Priest attained the principal aspect of clean garments, white garments. Through this he would atone for all Israel, as above.

breslov.he:
עיקר התגברות הבגדים צואים הוא בתאות ניאוף, ויוסף שהפשיט זה מעליו לגמרי זכה לכתונת פסים

״וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אָהַב אֶת יוֹסֵף וְגוֹ׳ וְעָשָׂה לוֹ כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים״

(לז, ג)

יוֹסֵף זָכָה בִּשְׁלֵמוּת לְהַפְשִׁיט מֵעַצְמוֹ הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים עַל יְדֵי שֶׁעָמַד בְּנִסָּיוֹן בְּנִדָּה שִׁפְחָה גּוֹיָה זוֹנָה שֶׁמִּשָּׁם עִקַּר הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים. וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ מֵחֲמַת שֶׁרָאָה צִדְקַת יוֹסֵף, עַל כֵּן ״וְעָשָׂה לוֹ כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים״ בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נָאִים, בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים. וְזֶה ״כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ וְעָשָׂה לוֹ כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים״. כִּי הוּא בָּרָא מַלְיָא, שֶׁמֵּחֲמַת שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ בֶּן זְקֻנִים בַּר חַכִּים שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶׁקִּבֵּל מִשֵּׁם וָעֵבֶר מָסַר לוֹ, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁמָּסַר לוֹ כָּל חָכְמָתוֹ וְתוֹרָתוֹ, עַל כֵּן ״וְעָשָׂה לוֹ כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים״ בְּחִינַת חֲלוּקָא דְּרַבָּנָן, בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים שֶׁזּוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה.

אֲבָל אֶחָיו נִתְקַנְּאוּ בּוֹ בָּזֶה. וְגַם רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה הִקְפִּידוּ עַל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ בָּזֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שבת דף י) ׳לְעוֹלָם אַל יְשַׁנֶּה אָדָם בְּנוֹ וְכוּ׳ שֶׁבִּשְׁבִיל מִשְׁקַל שְׁתֵּי סְלָעִים מֵילַת נִתְגַּלְגֵּל הַדָּבָר וְכוּ׳. הַיְנוּ שֶׁעֲדַיִן הָיָה קֹדֶם הַזְּמַן. כִּי עֲדַיִן הָיָה צָרִיךְ לַעֲבֹר עַל יוֹסֵף מַה שֶּׁעָבַר נִסְיוֹנוֹת רַבּוֹת. וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה צָרִיךְ לְהַמְתִּין מִלְּהַלְבִּישׁוֹ בִּכְתֹנֶת פַּסִּים עַד שֶׁיְּזַכֵּךְ עַצְמוֹ בִּשְׁלֵמוּת מִבְּחִינַת אֲחִיזַת הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיַּעֲבֹר בְּנִסָּיוֹן.

אחיו סברו שאינו נקי מזה ולכן התקנאו בזה והפשיטו ממנו כתנת זו

וּבִשְׁבִיל זֶה נִתְקַנְּאוּ בוֹ אֶחָיו, כִּי גַּם הֵם הָיוּ בַּעֲלֵי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְרָאוּ שֶׁעֲדַיִן הַבַּעַל דָּבָר מִתְגָּרֶה בּוֹ וְטָעוּ וְסָבְרוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ נָקִי כְּלָל מֵאֲחִיזַת הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים עַל כֵּן נִתְקַנְּאוּ עַל שֶׁעָשָׂה לוֹ אָבִיו כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים.

וְעַל כֵּן ״וַיַּפְשִׁיטוּ אֶת יוֹסֵף אֶת כֻּתָּנְתּוֹ אֶת כְּתֹנֶת הַפַּסִּים וְכוּ׳ וַיִּטְבְּלוּ אוֹתוֹ בְּדָם״, לְהוֹרוֹת שֶׁעֲדַיִן יֵשׁ בּוֹ אֲחִיזַת הַקִּלְקוּלִים הַנִּמְשָׁכִין מֵהַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים.

ולכן כשהביאו את הכתנת ליעקב מיד קשר את זה למלחמת אשת פוטיפר

וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁהֵבִיאוּ אֶת הַכְּתֹנֶת הַמְלֻכְלֶכֶת בְּדָם אֶל יַעֲקֹב אֲבִיהֶם, עַל כֵּן וַיֵּדַע יַעֲקֹב שֶׁמַּלְבּוּשׁ שָׁם בִּכְתָנָיו וְכוּ׳. וְאָז אָמַר, ״כְּתֹנֶת בְּנִי חַיָּה רָעָה אֲכָלָתְהוּ וְכוּ׳״ וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁנִּרְמַז שֶׁמִּתְגָּרֶה בּוֹ אִשָּׁה פּוֹטִיפַר. וְלִכְאוֹרָה תָּמוּהַּ הָעִנְיַן זֶה אֵצֶל זֶה, מַה עִנְיַן סְמִיכוֹת ״כְּתֹנֶת בְּנִי לְחַיָּה רָעָה אֲכָלָתְהוּ״ שֶׁהוּא עַל הִתְגָּרוּת אֵשֶׁת פּוֹטִיפַר.

אַךְ עַל פִּי הַנַּ״ל מְבֹאָר הֵיטֵב. כִּי תֵּכֶף כְּשֶׁרָאָה שֶׁכְּתֹנֶת יוֹסֵף מְלֻכְלֶכֶת בְּדָם אָז הֵבִין שֶׁעֲדַיִן מִתְגָּרִין בּוֹ הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים, שֶׁעִקַּר הִתְגָּרוּתָם בָּאָדָם הוּא בְּתַאֲוַת נִאוּף. וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר אָז כְּתֹנֶת בְּנִי חַיָּה רָעָה אֲכָלָתְהוּ שֶׁהִיא הִתְגָּרוּת אֵשֶׁת פּוֹטִיפַר שֶׁהִיא נִדָּה שִׁפְחָה גּוֹיָה זוֹנָה, שֶׁהֵם עִקַּר הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים כַּנַּ״ל.

וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם בְּעֵת הַנִּסָּיוֹן וַתִּתְפְּשֵׂהוּ בְּבִגְדוֹ. ׳בִּבְגְדוֹ׳ דַּיְקָא, כִּי רָצְתָה לְהִתְאַחֵז בְּבִגְדוֹ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְלַבֵּשׁ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בְּבְגָדִים צוֹאִים, אֲבָל יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק עָמַד בְּנִסָּיוֹן וְלֹא רָצָה לְטַמֹּאות נִשְׁמָתוֹ עַל יְדֵי בְּגָדִים צוֹאִים הַנִּמְשָׁכִין עַל יְדֵי נִאוּף. וְעַל כֵּן ״וַיַּעֲזֹב בִּגְדוֹ בְּיָדָהּ וַיָּנָס וַיֵּצֵא הַחוּצָה״. וְאָז דַּיְקָא בְּאוֹתָהּ הָרֶגַע הִפְשִׁיט מֵעַצְמוֹ בִּשְׁלֵמוּת כָּל אֲחִיזַת הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים שֶׁהָיוּ נֶאֱחָזִין בִּבְגָדָיו. כִּי אֲפִלּוּ הַצַּדִּיקִים הַגְּדוֹלִים כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא עָמְדוּ בַּנִּסָּיוֹן כָּרָאוּי לָהֶם עֲדַיִן יֵשׁ בָּהֶם אֵיזֶה אֲחִיזָה מֵהַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים. וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁעָבַר יוֹסֵף בַּנִּסָּיוֹן אָז דַּיְקָא הִפְשִׁיט מֵעַצְמוֹ בְּחִינַת אֲחִיזַת הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים בִּבְחִינַת וַיַּעֲזֹב בִּגְדוֹ בְּיָדָהּ וַיָּנָס וְכוּ׳. שֶׁהַבֶּגֶד שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ אֲחִיזָה בּוֹ עָזַב בְּיָדָהּ, וְהִפְשִׁיט אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִבְּגָדִים אֵלּוּ בִּשְׁלֵמוּת.

וְאָז זָכָה אַחַר כָּךְ לִבְגָדִים נְקִיִּים וִיקָרִים בִּבְחִינַת ״וַיַּלְבֵּשׁ אוֹתוֹ בִּגְדֵי שֵׁשׁ וְכוּ׳״. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ יוֹסֵף מִדִּלֵּהּ נָטַל וְכוּ׳. וּמִגֹּדֶל עֹצֶם צִדְקָתוֹ שֶׁעָמַד בַּנִּסָּיוֹן בָּזֶה זָכָה לְהַמְשִׁיךְ בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים לְכָל אֶחָיו בִּבְחִינַת לְכֻלָּם נָתַן לָאִישׁ חֲלִפוֹת שְׂמָלֹת וְכוּ׳. שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ כֹּחַ לְתַקֵּן כֻּלָּם לְהַמְשִׁיךְ לָהֶם בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים. וְעַל כֵּן וּלְבִנְיָמִן נָתַן וְכוּ׳ וְחָמֵשׁ חֲלִפֹת שְׂמָלֹת, שֶׁנִּרְמַז עַל בִּגְדֵי כֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁהָיָה מַחֲלִיף בְּגָדָיו חֲמִשָּׁה פְּעָמִים בְּיוֹם כִּפּוּר כְּשֶׁנִּכְנַס לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁהָיָה בָּנוּי בְּחֶלְקוֹ כַּמּוּבָא. כִּי עִקַּר בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים בְּגָדִים לְבָנִים זָכָה הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל. שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה מְכַפֵּר עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכַנַּ״ל.

(הלכות סעודה הלכה ה׳ אות מ׳)
breslov.en:
The principal prevailing of the soiled garments is in the desire for sexual immorality; and Yosef, who stripped this from himself entirely, merited the striped tunic.

“And Israel loved Yosef, etc., and made him a striped tunic.”

(37:3)

Yosef attained completely to stripping the soiled garments from himself through standing in the trial involving a menstruant woman, a bondwoman, a gentile woman, a harlot, from which the soiled garments chiefly come. And Yaakov our father, because he saw Yosef’s righteousness, therefore “made him a striped tunic,” the aspect of fine garments, clean garments. And this is “For he was a son of old age to him, and he made him a striped tunic.” For the one depends on the other [following the cited source; the anthology’s Hebrew differs]: because he had a son of old age, a wise son, to whom he transmitted all that he had received from Shem and Ever—namely, he transmitted all his wisdom and Torah to him—therefore “he made him a striped tunic,” the aspect of חלוקא דרבנן [the sages’ garment], the aspect of clean garments that are attained through Torah.

But his brothers envied him in this. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, also took issue with Yaakov our father about this, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Shabbos, folio 10), “A person should never treat his son differently,” etc., “for because of the weight of two selaim of fine wool the matter unfolded,” etc. Namely, it was still before the time, for what passed over Yosef—many trials—still had to pass over him. And therefore he needed to wait before clothing him in a striped tunic until [Yosef] purified himself completely from the aspect of the hold of the soiled garments through undergoing the trial.

His brothers thought that he was not clean of this; and therefore they envied him in this and stripped this tunic from him.

And because of this his brothers envied him, for they too possessed the holy spirit and saw that the adversary was still provoking him, and they erred and thought that he was not at all clean of the hold of the soiled garments. Therefore they envied him because his father had made him a striped tunic.

And therefore “and they stripped Yosef of his tunic, the striped tunic,” etc., “and dipped it in blood,” to indicate that he still had in him a hold of the corruptions that are drawn from the soiled garments.

And therefore, when they brought the tunic to Yaakov, he immediately connected this to the battle involving Potiphar’s wife.

And therefore, when they brought the blood-soiled tunic to Yaakov their father, therefore “and Yaakov tore his garments and put sackcloth on his loins,” etc. And then he said, “My son’s tunic—a wild animal has devoured him,” etc. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded that it was hinted that Potiphar’s wife was provoking him. And at first sight the placement of this matter beside that is puzzling: what is the matter of the juxtaposition of “my son’s tunic” to “a wild animal has devoured him,” which concerns the provocation of Potiphar’s wife?

But according to the above it is clearly explained. For immediately when he saw that Yosef’s tunic was soiled with blood, he understood that the soiled garments were still provoking him, for their principal provocation of a person is in the desire for sexual immorality. And therefore he then said, “My son’s tunic—a wild animal has devoured him,” which is the provocation of Potiphar’s wife, who is a menstruant woman, a bondwoman, a gentile woman, a harlot, which are the principal soiled garments, as above.

And this is what is written there at the time of the trial: “And she seized him by his garment.” “By his garment” specifically, for she wanted to gain a hold upon his garment, Heaven forbid, so that he would clothe himself, Heaven forbid, in soiled garments. But Yosef the tzaddik stood in the trial and did not want to defile his soul through soiled garments drawn through sexual immorality. And therefore “and he left his garment in her hand, and fled and went outside.” And then specifically, at that moment, he stripped from himself completely every hold of the soiled garments that had held onto his garments. For even the great tzaddikim, as long as they have not stood in the trial as is fitting for them, still have some hold of the soiled garments in them. And therefore, when Yosef passed through the trial, then specifically he stripped from himself the aspect of the hold of the soiled garments, in the aspect of “and he left his garment in her hand and fled,” etc. For the garment upon which she had a hold he left in her hand, and he stripped himself of these garments completely.

And then afterwards he attained clean and precious garments, in the aspect of “he clothed him in linen garments,” etc. And as is stated in the holy Zohar, “Yosef took from his own,” etc. And from the greatness of the might of his righteousness, that he stood in this trial, he attained to drawing the aspect of clean garments to all his brothers, in the aspect of “to all of them he gave each man changes of garments,” etc. This alludes to his having the power to rectify them all, to draw to them the aspect of clean garments. Therefore “and to Binyamin he gave,” etc., “five changes of garments,” which hints at the garments of the High Priest, who changed his garments five times on the Day of Atonement when he entered the Temple, which was built in his portion, as cited. For the High Priest attained the principal aspect of clean garments, white garments. Through this he would atone for all Israel, as above.

(Halachos of the Meal, Halacha 5, item 40)

pairs.he: כָּל מִינֵי מַחֲלֹקֶת נִמְשָׁכִין מִפְּגַם הָרָצוֹן עַל יְדֵי שֶׁאֵין מְקַשְּׁרִין כָּל הָרְצוֹנוֹת לְשֹׁרֶשׁ הָרָצוֹן, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת עִקַּר הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת הוּא מַחֲלֹקֶת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁחוֹלֵק עַל הָאָדָם וְרוֹצֶה לְהוֹרִידוֹ לִשְׁאוֹל תַּחְתִּיּוֹת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, וְעִקַּר הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הוּא בְּחִינַת חֲקִירוֹת וּכְפִירוֹת, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת חָלָק לֵבָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בְּמַאֲמַר וַיִּסֹּב אֱלֹקִים (סימן סב) עַיֵּן שָׁם. וּמִשָּׁם נִמְשָׁכִין כָּל הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם שֶׁכֻּלָּם בָּאִים מִבְּחִינַת מַחֲלֹקֶת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁשָּׁרְשׁוֹ כְּפִירוּת פְּגַם הָרָצוֹן.
pairs.en: All kinds of dispute are drawn from the blemish of will, through not binding all the wills to the root of will. For in truth the principal dispute is the dispute of the evil inclination, which disputes with a person and wishes to bring him down to the lowest Sheol, Heaven forbid. And the principal evil inclination is the aspect of investigations and denials, which is the aspect of “their heart is divided,” as Rabbainu, of blessed memory, wrote in the discourse “And God led around” (section 62); see there. And from there are drawn all the disputes in the world, which all come from the aspect of the dispute of the evil inclination, whose root is denial, the blemish of will.

pairs.he: כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת הוּא פְּגַם הָרָצוֹן, כִּי עִקַּר הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת הוּא בֵּין הָרְצוֹנוֹת, שֶׁזֶּה רְצוֹנוֹ כָּךְ וְזֶה רְצוֹנוֹ לְהֵפֶךְ, וּמֵחֲמַת זֶה נַעֲשֶׂה מַחֲלֹקֶת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם. וְכָל זֶה מֵחֲמַת שֶׁאֵין מְקַשְּׁרִין כָּל הָרְצוֹנוֹת לְשֹׁרֶשׁ הָרָצוֹן שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת רַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה, כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ מַחֲלֹקֶת שֶׁל הַסִּטְרָא אַחֲרָא שֶׁהֵם חַכְמֵי הַטֶּבַע שֶׁכּוֹפְרִים בָּרָצוֹן שֶׁזֶּה עִקַּר בְּחִינַת מַחֲלֹקֶת כַּנַּ״ל שָׁרְשָׁם מַחֲלֹקֶת שֶׁבִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁהוּא הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת שֶׁבֵּין הַצַּדִּיקִים הָאֲמִתִּיִּים, וּמִשָּׁם נִשְׁתַּלְשֵׁל הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת שֶׁל הַסִּטְרָא אַחֲרָא שֶׁהוּא כְּפִירוּת שֶׁל חַכְמֵי הַטֶּבַע, כַּמְבֹאָר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
pairs.en: For in truth dispute is the blemish of will, for the principal dispute is between the wills: this one’s will is thus and this one’s will is the opposite, and because of this dispute is made, Heaven forbid. And all this is because they do not bind all the wills to the root of will, which is the aspect of raava deraavin—the will of wills—the aspect of Moshe. For the root of the dispute of the other side, who are the sages of nature that deny will, which is the principal aspect of dispute as above—their root is dispute in holiness, which is the dispute among the true tzaddikim. And from there the dispute of the other side unfolds, which is the denial of the sages of nature, as explained elsewhere.

For the root of the dispute of the other side, who are the sages of nature that deny will, which is the principal aspect of dispute as above—their root is dispute in holiness, which is the dispute among the true tzaddikim. And from there the dispute of the other side unfolds, which is the denial of the sages of nature, as explained elsewhere.

pairs.he: מעולם לא היו שני צדיקים שוים לגמרי בדיעותיהם ומעשיהם
pairs.en: There have never been two tzaddikim entirely equal in their opinions and deeds.

qualifiedAfter.he: מעולם לא היו שני צדיקים שוים לגמרי בדיעותיהם ומעשיהם
qualifiedAfter.en: There have never been two tzaddikim entirely equal in their opinions and deeds.

pairs.he: וְעִקַּר הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת שֶׁבֵּין הַצַּדִּיקִים וְהַכְּשֵׁרִים הוּא מֵחֲמַת שֶׁאֵין מְקַשְּׁרִים כָּל הָרְצוֹנוֹת לְשֹׁרֶשׁ הָרָצוֹן שֶׁהוּא רַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה כַּנַּ״ל. כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַצַּדִּיקִים וְהַכְּשֵׁרִים כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד כַּוָּנָתוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן בְּוַדַּאי דַּעְתָּם מְחֻלָּק זֶה מִזֶּה, כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיוּ דֵּעוֹתֵיהֶם שָׁוֶה לְגַמְרֵי, כִּי אֵין שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם דּוֹמִים זֶה לָזֶה וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁמְּשֻׁנִּים בְּנֵי אָדָם בְּצוּרוֹתֵיהֶם כָּךְ מְשֻׁנִּים בְּדֵעוֹתֵיהֶם, וְעַל כֵּן בְּהֶכְרֵחַ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שִׁנּוּיִים בֵּינֵיהֶם בְּדֵעוֹתֵיהֶם וְדַרְכֵיהֶם וְהִתְנַהֲגוּתֵיהֶם. וּמִיּוֹם בְּרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם לֹא הָיוּ עֲדַיִן שְׁנֵי צַדִּיקִים כְּשֵׁרִים אֲמִתִּיִּים שָׁוִים לְגַמְרֵי בְּכָל הִתְנַהֲגוּתֵיהֶם אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם הוֹלְכִים בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶחָד וְיוֹנְקִים מֵרַב אֶחָד אַף עַל פִּי כֵן יֵשׁ חִלּוּקִים רַבִּים בְּדַרְכֵיהֶם וְהִתְנַהֲגוּתֵיהֶם.
pairs.en: And the principal dispute among the tzaddikim and upright people is because they do not bind all the wills to the root of will, which is raava deraavin, the aspect of Moshe, as above. For in truth each and every one of the tzaddikim and upright people has his intention and will for the sake of Heaven; and nevertheless their understandings certainly differ from one another, for it is impossible that their opinions should be entirely equal. For no two people resemble one another, and just as people differ in their forms, so they differ in their opinions. And therefore there must be differences between them in their opinions, ways, and conduct. And since the creation of the world there have not yet been two true, upright tzaddikim entirely equal in all their conduct; even though they both walk in one way and draw nourishment from one teacher, nevertheless there are many differences in their ways and conduct.

pairs.he: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהֶאֱרִיךְ רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה לְסַפֵּר וּלְהַפְלִיג בְּגֹדֶל הַחִלּוּקִים בֵּין הַצַּדִּיקִים הַגְּדוֹלִים שֶׁהָיוּ סְמוּכִים לִזְמַנֵּנוּ שֶׁכֻּלָּם הֵם מִתַּלְמִידֵי הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב וְהַמַּגִּיד זצוק״ל, וְהָיָה שָׁלוֹם גָּדוֹל בֵּינֵיהֶם, וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן הָיוּ מְחֻלָּקִים מְאֹד בְּדַרְכֵיהֶם. שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה נוֹסֵעַ עַל הַמְּדִינָה וְדָרַשׁ בָּרַבִּים, וְזֶה יָשַׁב בְּבֵיתוֹ, זֶה הֶאֱרִיךְ מְאֹד בִּתְפִלָּה וְהִתְפַּלֵּל לִפְנֵי הַתֵּבָה בְּצַעֲקוֹת וְהִתְלַהֲבוּת גָּדוֹל, וְזֶה הִתְפַּלֵּל בְּלַחַשׁ עִם הַצִּבּוּר כְּדֶרֶךְ הֶהָמוֹן, וְזֶה לָמַד הַרְבֵּה בַּתּוֹרָה יוֹתֵר, וְזֶה הִרְבָּה בִּצְדָקוֹת וּפִדְיוֹן שְׁבוּיִים, וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה שִׁנּוּיִים רַבִּים לְאֵין מִסְפָּר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכֻּלָּם יָנְקוּ מֵרַב אֶחָד.
pairs.en: And as Rabbainu, of blessed memory, expounded at length in telling and emphasizing the greatness of the differences among the great tzaddikim who were close to our time, who were all students of the Baal Shem Tov and the Maggid, of blessed holy and righteous memory, and there was great peace between them, yet they differed greatly in their ways. This one traveled about the country and preached publicly, and this one sat in his home; this one prolonged prayer greatly and prayed before the lectern with cries and great fervor, and this one prayed quietly with the congregation in the manner of the multitude; this one studied more Torah, and this one increased acts of charity and the redemption of captives; and likewise many differences without number, even though they all drew nourishment from one teacher.

This one traveled about the country and preached publicly, and this one sat in his home; this one prolonged prayer greatly and prayed before the lectern with cries and great fervor, and this one prayed quietly with the congregation in the manner of the multitude; this one studied more Torah, and this one increased acts of charity and the redemption of captives; and likewise many differences without number, even though they all drew nourishment from one teacher.

pairs.he: כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֻּלָּם שָׁוִין, כִּי כָּל אֶחָד עוֹבֵד אֶת ה׳ כְּפִי מַדְרֵגָתוֹ וּכְפִי שֹׁרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתוֹ. וְזֶה עִקַּר שַׁעֲשׁוּעָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ צַדִּיקִים וּכְשֵׁרִים הַרְבֵּה בָּעוֹלָם שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד עוֹשֶׂה לוֹ נַחַת רוּחַ וְתַעֲנוּג וְשַׁעֲשׁוּעַ מְיֻחָד מַה שֶּׁאֵין בַּחֲבֵרוֹ. שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר בְּךָ אֶתְפָּאָר שֶׁהֵם כְּלוּלִים מִגְּוָנִין סַגִּיאִין. כִּי אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים שָׁוִין, רַק כָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ וּנְתִיב כְּפִי שָׁרְשׁוֹ בָּרָצוֹן הָעֶלְיוֹן.
pairs.en: For it is impossible that they should all be equal, for each one serves the Lord according to his level and according to the root of his soul. And this is His principal delight, blessed be He: that He has many tzaddikim and upright people in the world, each and every one of whom gives Him a particular satisfaction, pleasure, and delight that is not in his fellow. This is the aspect of “Israel, in whom I shall glory,” for they comprise many colors. For the Holy One, blessed be He, does not make two things equal; rather, each one has a way and a path according to his root in the upper will.

pairs.he: אֲבָל הַבַּעַל דָּבָר הוּא מִתְגָּרֶה וּמִתְקַנֵּא בַּחֲבוּרוֹת הַצַּדִּיקִים וְהַכְּשֵׁרִים וּמַכְנִיס בָּהֶם מַחֲלֹקֶת. וְעִקַּר הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת הוּא מֵחֲמַת שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד אֵינוֹ מַאֲמִין בַּחֲבֵרוֹ שֶׁגַּם כַּוָּנָתוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין חֲבֵרוֹ מִתְנַהֵג בְּדַרְכּוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ, כִּי הַבַּעַל דָּבָר מַטְעֶה הַלֵּב עַד שֶׁנִּדְמֶה לְכָל אֶחָד שֶׁחֲבֵרוֹ חוֹלֵק עָלָיו וְנוֹטֶה מִן הָאֱמֶת, כִּי הַבַּעַל דָּבָר הוּא נִרְגָּן מַפְרִיד אַלּוּף וְאִישׁ מְדָנִים לְחַרְחֵר רִיב, כִּי הוֹלֵךְ וּמְסַכְסֵךְ זֶה בָּזֶה וְהוּא בֵּין אַחִים יַפְרִיא.
pairs.en: But the adversary provokes and envies the companies of tzaddikim and upright people and brings dispute among them. And the principal dispute is because each one does not believe of his fellow that his intention and will too are for the sake of Heaven, even though his fellow does not conduct himself in his way and will. For the adversary misleads the heart until it seems to each one that his fellow disputes with him and deviates from the truth. For the adversary is a whisperer who separates a close companion and a man of contentions who stirs strife; for he goes and sets this one against that one, and he “yafri” between brothers [candidate printed terminal verb, unresolved].

pairs.he: עַד שֶׁלִּפְעָמִים יֵשׁ שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם רוֹצִים רָצוֹן אֶחָד, וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן יֵשׁ בֵּינֵיהֶם מַחֲלֹקֶת גָּדוֹל, מֵחֲמַת שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁחֲבֵרוֹ רוֹצֶה גַּם כֵּן בָּזֶה, וְאֵינָם מִתְוַעֲדִים יַחַד לְדַבֵּר אֶחָד עִם חֲבֵרוֹ לְגַלּוֹת דַּעְתּוֹ וּפְנִימִיּוּת רְצוֹנוֹ, וּמֵחֲמַת זֶה נִדְמֶה לַחֲבֵרוֹ שֶׁהוּא אֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה בָּזֶה וּמֵחֲמַת זֶה נַעֲשֶׂה בֵּינֵיהֶם מַחֲלֹקֶת גָּדוֹל. עַד שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ אֲפִלּוּ כְּשֶׁמִּתְוַעֲדִים יַחַד, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְכָל אֶחָד לְגַלּוֹת לַחֲבֵרוֹ פְּנִימִיּוּת דַּעְתּוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ, כִּי מֵחֲמַת הַקְּטָטוֹת וְהַמְּרִיבוֹת וְהַהַקְפָּדוֹת שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם אֵין אֶחָד מֵהֶם יוֹדֵעַ וּמֵבִין רְצוֹן חֲבֵרוֹ שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת אֵין שׁוּם שִׁנּוּי בֵּינֵיהֶם. וְדָבָר זֶה מָצוּי בְּכָל פַּעַם כַּיָּדוּעַ.
pairs.en: Until sometimes there are two people who both desire one will, and nevertheless there is great dispute between them, because each one does not know that his fellow also wishes this, and they do not meet together to speak with one another to reveal his understanding and the inwardness of his will. And because of this it seems to his fellow that he does not wish this, and because of this great dispute arises between them. Until afterwards, even when they meet together, it is impossible for each one to reveal to his fellow the inwardness of his understanding and will; for because of the quarrels, contentions, and resentments between them, neither of them knows and understands his fellow’s will, when in truth there is no difference at all between them. And this thing is found every time, as is known.

pairs.he: וְהַכְּלָל שֶׁעִקַּר הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת מֵחֲמַת שִׁנּוּי הָרְצוֹנוֹת, וְכָל זֶה מֵחֲמַת שֶׁאֵין מְקַשְּׁרִין כָּל הָרְצוֹנוֹת לְשֹׁרֶשׁ הָרָצוֹן שֶׁהוּא רָצוֹן שֶׁבָּרְצוֹנוֹת.
pairs.en: And the rule is that the principal dispute is because of the difference of wills, and all this is because they do not bind all the wills to the root of will, which is the will within the wills.

pairs.he: צריך לדון את חבירו שדעתו אחרת שגם כוונתו לשמים
pairs.en: One must judge his fellow, whose understanding differs, as having his intention too directed to Heaven.

qualifiedAfter.he: צריך לדון את חבירו שדעתו אחרת שגם כוונתו לשמים
qualifiedAfter.en: One must judge his fellow, whose understanding differs, as having his intention too directed to Heaven.

pairs.he: כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת רָאוּי לֵידַע שֶׁכָּל הָרְצוֹנוֹת שֶׁל כָּל בְּנֵי הָאָדָם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בֵּינֵיהֶם שִׁנּוּיִים גְּדוֹלִים, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן כֻּלָּם נִמְשָׁכִין מֵרָצוֹן הָעֶלְיוֹן שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שׁוּם שִׁנּוּי שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת רָצוֹן שֶׁבָּרְצוֹנוֹת, רַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין. וּמִי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ וּמַאֲמִין בָּזֶה בִּשְׁלֵמוּת, בְּוַדַּאי לֹא יַחֲזִיק בְּמַחֲלֹקֶת, כִּי יָדִין אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ לְכַף זְכוּת תָּמִיד, כִּי יֹאמַר בְּלִבּוֹ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֲנִי יוֹדֵעַ בְּעַצְמִי שֶׁכַּוָּנָתִי לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם לִגְמֹר מִצְוָה הַזֹּאת וְחֶפְצִי שָׁמַיִם בֶּאֱמֶת, וַחֲבֵרִי מְעַכֵּב מִזֶּה, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן גַּם כַּוָּנָתוֹ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, רַק יֵשׁ לוֹ דֵּעָה אַחֶרֶת וְנִדְמֶה לוֹ שֶׁאֵין זֶה מִצְוָה כְּלָל, אוֹ צְרִיכִין לַעֲסֹק בְּמִצְוָה אַחֶרֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה מִזֹּאת לְפִי דַּעְתּוֹ.
pairs.en: For in truth one ought to know that all the wills of all people, although there are great differences between them, nevertheless are all drawn from the upper will, in which there is no difference at all, which is the aspect of the will within the wills, raava deraavin. And one who knows and believes this completely will certainly not hold onto dispute, for he will always judge his fellow favorably. For he will say in his heart: although I know within myself that my intention is for the sake of Heaven, to complete this commandment, and I truly desire heavenly matters, and my fellow prevents this, nevertheless his intention too is for the sake of Heaven. Only he has a different opinion, and it seems to him that this is no commandment at all, or that one needs to occupy oneself with another commandment greater than this, according to his understanding.

pairs.he: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֲנִי חָזָק בְּדַעְתִּי מְאֹד וְיֵשׁ לִי רְאָיוֹת וְהוֹכָחוֹת אֲמִתִּיּוֹת שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לְהַחֲזִיק בְּיוֹתֵר בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה וּבְמִצְוָה הַזֹּאת, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן אֲפִלּוּ אִם הָאֱמֶת הוּא כְּדַעְתִּי, מִי יוֹדֵעַ מֵאֵיזֶה שֹׁרֶשׁ נִמְשָׁךְ חֲבֵרִי. אֶפְשָׁר לְפִי שֹׁרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתוֹ הוּא צָרִיךְ לְהִתְנַהֵג בְּדֶרֶךְ אַחֵר. כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת כָּל הַדֵּעוֹת וְהָרְצוֹנוֹת נִמְשָׁכִין מֵרָצוֹן הָעֶלְיוֹן רַק שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהָבִין זֹאת.
pairs.en: And although I am very firm in my understanding, and I have true evidence and proofs that one needs to hold especially firmly to this way and this commandment, nevertheless, even if the truth is according to my understanding, who knows from which root my fellow is drawn? Perhaps according to the root of his soul he needs to conduct himself in a different way. For in truth all the opinions and wills are drawn from the upper will; only it is impossible to understand this.

pairs.he: וְאִם כָּל אֶחָד יֹאמַר בְּלִבּוֹ כֵּן בְּוַדַּאי יִתְבַּטֵּל הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת, כִּי עִקַּר הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת הוּא מֵחֲמַת שֶׁאֵין מְקַשְּׁרִין כָּל הָרְצוֹנוֹת לָרָצוֹן הָעֶלְיוֹן שֶׁשָּׁם כֻּלּוֹ חַד וְשָׁם כֻּלּוֹ שָׁלוֹם כִּי הַכֹּל נִכְלָל בְּאֶחָד. וְעַל כֵּן עִקַּר הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַצַּדִּיק הַדּוֹר הַגָּדוֹל בְּמַעֲלָה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה שֶׁנִּשְׁמָתוֹ מִבְּחִינַת רַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין, רָצוֹן שֶׁבָּרְצוֹנוֹת שֶׁהוּא יוֹדֵעַ רְצוֹן כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד וּמֵהֵיכָן הוּא נִמְשָׁךְ וְעַל כֵּן הוּא אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר רוּחַ בּוֹ שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לַהֲלֹךְ נֶגֶד רוּחוֹ שֶׁל כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד כִּי יוֹדֵעַ רוּחוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד וְיוֹדֵעַ לְקַשֵּׁר וּלְיַחֵד רוּחוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד בְּשֹׁרֶשׁ הָרָצוֹן וְשָׁם מְיַחֵד וּמְקַשֵּׁר כֻּלָּם בְּרָצוֹן אֶחָד הָעֶלְיוֹן. וְאָז נִמְשָׁךְ אַהֲבָה וְשָׁלוֹם גָּדוֹל וְנִפְלָא בֵּינֵיהֶם מֵאַחַר שֶׁכֻּלָּם בְּדֵעוֹתֵיהֶם וּרְצוֹנוֹתֵיהֶם הַמְשֻׁנּוֹת מְקֻשָּׁרִים וּמְיֻחָדִים בָּרָצוֹן אֶחָד הָעֶלְיוֹן שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שׁוּם שִׁנּוּי שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת רַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And if each one says thus in his heart, dispute will certainly be nullified. For the principal dispute is because they do not bind all the wills to the upper will, where all is one and all is peace, for everything is incorporated into one. And therefore the principal peace is through the tzaddik of the generation, great in stature, who is the aspect of Moshe, whose soul is from the aspect of raava deraavin, the will within the wills. He knows the will of each and every one and from where it is drawn, and therefore he is a man in whom there is spirit, who knows how to walk in accordance with the spirit of each and every one. For he knows the spirit and will of each and every one and knows how to bind and unify the spirit and will of each and every one at the root of will; and there he unifies and binds them all in the one upper will. And then great and wondrous love and peace are drawn between them, since all of them, in their differing opinions and wills, are bound and unified in the one upper will, in which there is no difference at all, which is the aspect of raava deraavin, as above.

pairs.he: וּבְכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר נִמְצָא צַדִּיק כָּזֶה שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לַהֲלֹךְ נֶגֶד רוּחוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ הָיָה נַעֲשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיוּ הַכֹּל שָׁבִים לַה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי הַכֹּל תָּלוּי בְּשָׁלוֹם, כַּמְבֹאָר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר. כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַשָּׁלוֹם יְכוֹלִים לִמְשֹׁךְ כָּל הָעוֹלָם לַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת רָצוֹן וְאַהֲבָה וְאַחְדוּת עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִכְלָלִין בָּרָצוֹן הָאֶחָד הָעֶלְיוֹן וְנִתְבַּטְּלִים כָּל כֹּחוֹת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁיְּנִיקָתוֹ מִבְּחִינַת שִׁנּוּי רְצוֹנוֹת שֶׁמִּשָּׁם יוֹנֵק וּמַכְנִיס כְּפִירוֹת וּמַחֲלֹקֶת כִּי הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע נִקְרָא מַחֲלֹקֶת, וּבִטּוּל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַשָּׁלוֹם וְעַל כֵּן גָּדוֹל הַשָּׁלוֹם מְאֹד כְּמוֹ שֶׁהִפְלִיגוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת.
pairs.en: And in each and every generation such a tzaddik is found, who knows how to walk in accordance with the spirit and will of each and every one, through whom peace would be made in the world, and through this everyone would return to the Lord, blessed be He. For everything depends upon peace, as explained elsewhere. For through peace the whole world can be drawn to His service; for through peace, which is the aspect of will, love, and unity, through this they are incorporated into the one upper will, and all the powers of the evil inclination are nullified. Its nourishment is from the aspect of differing wills, from where it draws nourishment and introduces denials and dispute, for the evil inclination is called dispute. And the nullification of the evil inclination is through peace; and therefore peace is very great, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, emphasized in several places.

pairs.he: אֲבָל כְּשֶׁרוֹאֶה הַבַּעַל דָּבָר שֶׁנִּמְצָא צַדִּיק כָּזֶה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת רַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין שֶׁיָּכוֹל לַעֲשׂוֹת שָׁלוֹם בֵּין הַכֹּל אֲזַי הוּא מְעוֹרֵר מַחֲלֹקֶת גָּדוֹל עַל זֶה הַצַּדִּיק הַגָּדוֹל בְּעַצְמוֹ עַד שֶׁהַכֹּל חוֹלְקִין עָלָיו בְּיוֹתֵר מֵעַל כָּל הָעוֹלָם, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל רְחוֹקִים מִמֶּנּוּ, כִּי כָּל אֶחָד רָחוֹק מֵחֲבֵרוֹ מֵחֲמַת שִׁנּוּי הָרְצוֹנוֹת שֶׁבֵּינוֹ וּבֵין חֲבֵרוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַאֲמִין שֶׁשְּׁנֵי הָרְצוֹנוֹת כְּלוּלִים בְּאֶחָד בְּשָׁרְשָׁם אֲבָל הַשִּׁנּוּי וְהָרִחוּק שֶׁבֵּין אָדָם לַחֲבֵרוֹ הוּא מְעַט מְאֹד כִּי בְּרֹב דַּרְכֵיהֶם הֵם שָׁוִין זֶה לָזֶה בְּתַאֲוֹתֵיהֶן וּמִדּוֹתֵיהֶן רַק שֶׁיֵּשׁ אֵיזֶה רִחוּק וְשִׁנּוּי בֵּינֵיהֶם.
pairs.en: But when the adversary sees that such a tzaddik is found, who is the aspect of raava deraavin and can make peace between everyone, then he arouses great dispute against this great tzaddik himself, until everyone disputes with him more than with anyone in the world. For in truth everyone is distant from him. For each person is distant from his fellow because of the difference of wills between him and his fellow, as he does not believe that the two wills are incorporated into one at their roots. But the difference and distance between a person and his fellow is very little, for in most of their ways they resemble one another in their desires and traits; only there is some distance and difference between them.

pairs.he: אֲבָל מִזֶּה הַצַּדִּיק הַגָּדוֹל הַכֹּל רְחוֹקִים לְגַמְרֵי, כִּי הוּא מְרוּמָם וּמְנֻשָּׂא מִכָּל שִׁנּוּי הָרְצוֹנוֹת שֶׁל כָּל בְּנֵי הָעוֹלָם כִּי הוּא רָחוֹק לְגַמְרֵי מִכָּל הָעוֹלָם וְאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם רָצוֹן בָּזֶה הָעוֹלָם כְּלָל רַק הוּא כָּלוּל תָּמִיד בָּרָצוֹן הָעֶלְיוֹן בִּבְחִינַת רַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין וּמִי שֶׁמַּאֲמִין בּוֹ וּמִתְקָרֵב אֵלָיו אֲזַי כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד יָכוֹל לִמְצֹא אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּתוֹךְ זֶה הַצַּדִּיק, כִּי הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ נִשְׁמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכָלוּל מִכֻּלָּם, כִּי הוּא בְּחִינַת רָצוֹן שֶׁבָּרְצוֹנוֹת הַיְנוּ הָרָצוֹן הָעֶלְיוֹן הַמִּכְלַל בְּכָל הָרְצוֹנוֹת וְהַנְּפָשׁוֹת שֶׁל כָּל בְּנֵי עוֹלָם. אֲבָל כְּשֶׁהַבַּעַל דָּבָר מַכְנִיס כְּפִירוֹת וּמַחֲלֹקֶת בְּלֵב בְּנֵי אָדָם לַחֲלֹק עָלָיו אֲזַי הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת עָלָיו גָּדוֹל יוֹתֵר מִכָּל מִינֵי מַחֲלֹקֶת מֵחֲמַת שֶׁהוּא רָחוֹק וּמְרוּמָם מִכָּל הָרְצוֹנוֹת שֶׁל כָּל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם שֶׁכֻּלָּם יֵשׁ בָּהֶם שִׁנּוּיִים וְהוּא אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם שִׁנּוּי רָצוֹן שֶׁל זֶה הָעוֹלָם. וְעַל כֵּן כֻּלָּם חוֹלְקִים עָלָיו וְאֵין יְכוֹלִים לְסָבְלוֹ.
pairs.en: But everyone is entirely distant from this great tzaddik, for he is exalted and raised above all the differences of wills of all people of the world, for he is entirely distant from the whole world and has no will in this world at all; rather, he is continually incorporated into the upper will, in the aspect of raava deraavin. And one who believes in him and draws near to him—then each and every one can find himself within this tzaddik, for he is the root of the soul of Israel and comprises them all. For he is the aspect of the will within the wills—namely, the upper will included within all the wills and souls of all people of the world. But when the adversary introduces denials and dispute into people’s hearts to dispute with him, then the dispute against him is greater than all kinds of dispute, because he is distant and exalted above all the wills of all who come into the world, all of whom have differences within them, whereas he has no differing will of this world at all. And therefore everyone disputes with him and cannot tolerate him.

pairs.he: זה היה ענין המחלוקת על יוסף הצדיק
pairs.en: This was the matter of the dispute against Yosef the tzaddik.

qualifiedAfter.he: זה היה ענין המחלוקת על יוסף הצדיק
qualifiedAfter.en: This was the matter of the dispute against Yosef the tzaddik.

pairs.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת שֶׁל הַשְּׁבָטִים עַל יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, כִּי יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק הוּא בְּחִינַת הַצַּדִּיק הַנַּ״ל בְּחִינַת רַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין, בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה, כִּי יוֹסֵף מֹשֶׁה וְדָוִד כֻּלָּם בְּחִינָה אַחַת שֶׁנִּסְתַּלְּקוּ שְׁלָשְׁתָּם בְּשַׁבָּת בְּמִנְחָה בְּרַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין, וְכָל הַשְּׁבָטִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכֻּלָּם הָיוּ צַדִּיקִים גְּדוֹלִים וְנוֹרָאִים, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן הָיוּ צְרִיכִין כֻּלָּם לְהִתְקַשֵּׁר אֵלָיו שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הִתְקַשְּׁרוּת כָּל הָרְצוֹנוֹת לְשֹׁרֶשׁ הָרָצוֹן שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַזָּקֵן שֶׁבִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ, בֶּן זְקֻנִים דַּיְקָא הַיְנוּ שֶׁשָּׁרְשׁוֹ בְּחִינַת זָקֵן שֶׁבִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת מֵצַח הָרָצוֹן, בְּחִינַת רַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And this is the aspect of the dispute of the tribes against Yosef the tzaddik, for Yosef the tzaddik is the aspect of the tzaddik mentioned above, the aspect of raava deraavin, the aspect of Moshe. For Yosef, Moshe, and Dovid are all one aspect, for all three departed on Shabbos at the afternoon prayer, at raava deraavin. And all the holy tribes, although they were all great and awesome tzaddikim, nevertheless all needed to bind themselves to him, which is the aspect of binding all the wills to the root of will, which is the aspect of the holy elder, the aspect of Yosef the tzaddik. As it is written, “For he was a son of old age to him”—“son of old age” specifically, namely, his root was the aspect of a holy elder, which is the aspect of the forehead of will, the aspect of raava deraavin, as above.

qualifiedAfter.en: And this is the aspect of the dispute of the tribes against Yosef the tzaddik, for Yosef the tzaddik is the aspect of the tzaddik mentioned above, the aspect of raava deraavin, the aspect of Moshe. pairs.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת מַה שֶּׁסִּפֵּר לָהֶם יוֹסֵף חֲלוֹמוֹ, וְהִנֵּה אֲנַחְנוּ מְאַלְּמִים אֲלֻמִּים בְּתוֹךְ הַשָּׂדֶה וְהִנֵּה קָמָה אֲלֻמָּתִי וְכוּ׳ וְהִנֵּה תְסֻבֶּינָה אֲלֻמּוֹתֵיכֶם וַתִּשְׁתַּחֲוֶיןָ לַאֲלֻמָּתִי. כִּי כָּל הַשְּׁבָטִים שֶׁהֵם כְּלָלִיּוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַשְּׁרִים קְשָׁרִים וּמְיַחֲדִים יִחוּדִים שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הִתְקַשְּׁרוּת הָרְצוֹנוֹת יַחַד, אֲבָל כָּל הַקְּשָׁרִים וְהַיִּחוּדִים צְרִיכִין לָבוֹא לְהַצַּדִּיק הַדּוֹר שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת רַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין שֶׁהוּא מְקַשֵּׁר כָּל הַקְּשָׁרִים וְהַיִּחוּדִים לָרָצוֹן הָעֶלְיוֹן, בִּבְחִינַת וְהִנֵּה תְסֻבֶּינָה אֲלֻמּוֹתֵיכֶם וַתִּשְׁתַּחֲוֶיןָ לַאֲלֻמָּתִי.
pairs.en: And this is the aspect of what Yosef told them of his dream: “And behold, we are binding sheaves within the field, and behold, my sheaf arose,” etc., “and behold, your sheaves came around and bowed to my sheaf.” For all the tribes, which are the totality of Israel, bind bonds and effect unifications, which is the aspect of binding the wills together. But all the bonds and unifications must come to the tzaddik of the generation, who is the aspect of Yosef, the aspect of raava deraavin, who binds all the bonds and unifications to the upper will, in the aspect of “And behold, your sheaves came around and bowed to my sheaf.”

pairs.he: וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה הַחֲלוֹם בְּעִנְיַן עֲבוֹדַת הַשָּׂדֶה, כִּי תִּקּוּן עֲבוֹדַת הַשָּׂדֶה הוּא עַל יְדֵי הֶאָרַת הָרָצוֹן שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְבַּטְּלִין כָּל הַל״ט מְלָאכוֹת, כִּי נִתְקַיֵּם הָעוֹלָם בְּחַסְדּוֹ וְכוּ׳, כַּמְבֹאָר בְּהַתּוֹרָה הַנַּ״ל. (ועיין מזה לעיל בהלכות ערב הלכה ג שם מבאר ענין זה היטב). וְעַל כֵּן גִּלָּה לָהֶם שֶׁתִּקּוּן עֲבוֹדַת הַשָּׂדֶה לְבַטֵּל זֻהֲמַת הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁנִּתְקַלְּלָה הָאֲדָמָה עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּזֵעַת אַפֶּךָ תֹּאכַל לֶחֶם וְכוּ׳ וּלְבַטֵּל כָּל זֶה שֶׁזֶּה תָּלוּי עַל יְדֵי הֶאָרַת הָרָצוֹן, כַּמְבֹאָר לְעֵיל בְּהִלְכוֹת עָרֵב, עַיֵּן שָׁם. וְכָל זֶה תָּלוּי בְּיוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת רָצוֹן שֶׁבָּרְצוֹנוֹת כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And therefore the dream concerned work of the field, for the rectification of work of the field is through the illumination of will, through which all the thirty-nine labors are nullified, for the world is sustained by His kindness, etc., as explained in the Torah teaching mentioned above. (And see about this above in Halachos of a Guarantor, Halacha 3; there this matter is clearly explained.) And therefore he revealed to them that the rectification of work of the field is to nullify the filth of the serpent, on account of which the ground was cursed, “By the sweat of your brow you shall eat bread,” etc., and to nullify all this, which depends upon the illumination of will, as explained above in Halachos of a Guarantor; see there. And all this depends upon Yosef, who is the aspect of the will within the wills, as above.

pairs.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת הַחֲלוֹם הַשֵּׁנִי וְהִנֵּה הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְהַיָּרֵחַ וְאַחַד עָשָׂר כּוֹכָבִים מִשְׁתַּחֲוִים לִי, הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְהַיָּרֵחַ וְאַחַד עָשָׂר כּוֹכָבִים הַמִּשְׁתַּחֲוִים לְיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת רַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין כַּנַּ״ל זֶה בְּחִינַת בִּטּוּל הַטֶּבַע, כִּי כָּל חָכְמַת הַטֶּבַע הוּא עַל פִּי מַעֲרֶכֶת הַמַּזָּלוֹת עַל פִּי הִלּוּךְ הַגַּלְגַּלִּים שֶׁל הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְהַיָּרֵחַ וְהַכּוֹכָבִים וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב שָׁם רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בְּהַתּוֹרָה הַנַּ״ל עַל פָּסוּק שִׂימוּ אוֹתָם אוֹתוֹת שֶׁאוֹמְרִים שֶׁהַכֹּל עַל יְדֵי אוֹתוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְחַס וְשָׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא הַטֶּבַע. אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל עַל יְדֵי רְצוֹנוֹ לְבַד יִתְבָּרַךְ וְהַטֶּבַע בְּעַצְמָהּ מִתְנַהֶגֶת רַק בִּרְצוֹנוֹ לְבַד יִתְבָּרַךְ וּכְמַצְבְּיֵהּ עֲבִיד בְּחֵיל שְׁמַיָּא וְאַרְעָא כִּי הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְהַיָּרֵחַ וְהַכּוֹכָבִים שֶׁמֵּהֶם נִמְשָׁךְ הַטֶּבַע כֻּלָּם מִתְנַהֲגִים רַק בָּרָצוֹן הָעֶלְיוֹן שֶׁמִּשָּׁם שֹׁרֶשׁ יוֹסֵף כַּנַּ״ל בִּבְחִינַת וְהִנֵּה הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְהַיָּרֵחַ וְאַחַד עָשָׂר כּוֹכָבִים מִשְׁתַּחֲוִים לִי, כִּי הַטֶּבַע מִתְנַהֶגֶת רַק בָּרָצוֹן הָעֶלְיוֹן שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת רַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין שֶׁמִּשָּׁם שֹׁרֶשׁ נִשְׁמַת יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And this is the aspect of the second dream, “And behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars bow to me.” The sun and moon and eleven stars that bow to Yosef the tzaddik, who is the aspect of raava deraavin, as above—this is the aspect of the nullification of nature. For all the wisdom of nature is according to the arrangement of the constellations, according to the course of the spheres of the sun, moon, and stars. And as Rabbainu, of blessed memory, wrote there in the Torah teaching mentioned above concerning the verse “They set them as signs”: they say that everything is through the signs of Heaven, and, Heaven forbid, that it is nature. But in truth everything is through His will alone, blessed be He; and nature itself is conducted only through His will alone, blessed be He, “and according to His desire He acts among the host of heaven and earth.” For the sun, moon, and stars, from which nature is drawn, are all conducted only by the upper will, from where Yosef’s root is, as above, in the aspect of “And behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars bow to me.” For nature is conducted only by the upper will, which is the aspect of raava deraavin, from where the root of the soul of Yosef the tzaddik is, as above.

qualifiedAfter.en: And this is the aspect of the second dream, “And behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars bow to me.” The sun and moon and eleven stars that bow to Yosef the tzaddik, who is the aspect of raava deraavin, as above—this is the aspect of the nullification of nature. For all the wisdom of nature is according to the arrangement of the constellations, according to the course of the spheres of the sun, moon, and stars. And as Rabbainu, of blessed memory, wrote there in the Torah teaching mentioned above concerning the verse “They set them as signs”: they say that everything is through the signs of Heaven, and, Heaven forbid, that it is nature. But in truth everything is through His will alone, blessed be He; and nature itself is conducted only through His will alone, blessed be He, “and according to His desire He acts among the host of heaven and earth.” For the sun, moon, and stars, from which nature is drawn, are all conducted only by the upper will, from where Yosef’s root is, as above, in the aspect of “And behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars bow to me.” For nature is conducted only by the upper will, which is the aspect of raava deraavin, from where the root of the soul of Yosef the tzaddik is, as above.
